name: Epoch AI - ECI Benchmarking Hub (raw per-model per-benchmark performance)
metric: performance (benchmark-native score, mostly 0-1 normalized accuracy/pass-rate; scale varies by benchmark)
how_to_parse: GET the URL (301-redirects to /data/processed_data_for_eci.csv, follow automatically). Plain CSV with header model_id,benchmark_id,performance,benchmark,benchmark_release_date,model,model_version,Model,date,source. Use model_version as the published model id when present (carries reasoning-effort suffixes like kimi-k3_low/kimi-k3_max), else fall back to the model column. Map the benchmark column to one of our four skills with an explicit lookup table (coding benchmarks -> code, GPQA/HLE/MMLU/math/trivia -> reasoning, SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench/OSWorld/agent benchmarks -> agentic, writing-preference benchmarks -> chat); unrecognized benchmark names default to reasoning and are flagged.
license_or_terms_note: Epoch AI states its benchmarking data is free to use, distribute and reproduce provided the source and authors are credited (CC BY). No key, no login.

name: LiveBench (new-livebench) per-subtask score table
format: csv (discovered via GitHub contents API JSON)
how_to_parse: GET the GitHub contents API for the public/ directory of LiveBench/new-livebench, regex-match files named table_YYYY_MM_DD.csv, pick the max date, then GET that raw CSV. First column is model id, remaining columns are per-subtask scores. Map subtask columns to skills: code={code_completion,code_generation,javascript,python,typescript}, reasoning={AMPS_Hard,connections,integrals_with_game,logic_with_navigation,math_comp,olympiad,spatial,theory_of_mind,zebra_puzzle}, chat={paraphrase,story_generation,summarize,typos}, agentic={consecutive_events,plot_unscrambling,tablejoin,tablereformat}. Emit one row per (model, subtask).
license_or_terms_note: Repo issue #53 discusses licensing of the table_*.csv files; treated here as a public, freely downloadable data table on a public GitHub repo (no login, no key). Re-verify license text if redistributing beyond internal router use.

name: Aider polyglot coding leaderboard (per-run results)
format: yaml (flat list of flat dicts - parsed with a small hand-rolled line parser, no PyYAML available in stdlib)
metric: pass_rate_2 (percent of 225 exercises solved, second attempt allowed) and seconds_per_case (wall-clock latency per exercise)
how_to_parse: GET raw YAML. Each entry starts with a '- dirname:' line followed by 2-space-indented 'key: value' lines until the next '- dirname:' or EOF; no nested lists/maps or block scalars are present in this file, so a regex line parser is safe. Emit two rows per entry when fields exist: (benchmark=aider_polyglot_pass_rate_2, skill=code, score=pass_rate_2) and (benchmark=aider_polyglot_seconds_per_case, skill=speed, score=seconds_per_case, higher_is_better=false).
license_or_terms_note: Public data file in the Aider-AI/aider open-source (Apache-2.0) GitHub repo. No key, no login.

name: SWE-bench Verified leaderboard
metric: resolved (percent of Verified instances resolved by an agent+model submission)
how_to_parse: GET the JSON, take leaderboards[] entry where name=='Verified', for each result use model_display as model_name_as_published and resolved as the score. Note: SWE-bench scores are agent-scaffold-dependent, not pure model scores - the same model can appear many times with different scaffolds/scores.
license_or_terms_note: Public data file in the SWE-bench/swe-bench.github.io open-source GitHub repo. No key, no login.

name: LMArena (Chatbot Arena) - Text arena, overall category
format: json (Hugging Face datasets-server rows API, paginated)
how_to_parse: GET paginated rows (offset/length=100) from the official lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset HF dataset, config=text, split=latest; keep rows where category=='overall'; stop paginating once a full page returns no 'overall' rows (the block is contiguous at the start of the split). model_name_as_published = model_name field, score = rating.
license_or_terms_note: Dataset is published by lmarena-ai under license cc-by-4.0 on the Hugging Face Hub. datasets-server is Hugging Face's public read API, no key or login required.

name: LMArena (Chatbot Arena) - Text arena, style-controlled rating, overall category
format: json (Hugging Face datasets-server rows API, paginated)

name: LMArena - WebDev Arena (coding preference), overall category
format: json (Hugging Face datasets-server rows API, paginated)
metric: rating (Elo-style arena rating for generated web apps)
how_to_parse: Same pagination approach as lmarena_text but config=webdev.

name: LMArena - Agent arena (tool-use / agentic tasks), overall category
how_to_parse: Single page GET (46 total rows), category=='overall', model_name_as_published = model_name, score = score field. Note: model_name in this config is Title Case with parenthetical effort tags e.g. 'Claude Fable 5.1 (Max)', inconsistent with the kebab-case ids used in text/webdev configs - a name-matching pitfall.

name: Artificial Analysis - Intelligence Index / Coding Index / speed (tokens/s) / latency
skill: mixed (would give reasoning 'Intelligence Index', code 'Coding Index', and speed tokens/s + TTFT latency in one place)
license_or_terms_note: Official API requires an x-api-key header (free tier exists: ~1000 requests/day per public docs, but still requires signup to obtain a key). Per task rules (no API keys, no signups), this was NOT scraped or called. This is the single most useful missing source for the 'speed/latency' skill - nothing else found gives per-model tokens/s or time-to-first-token without a key.

name: OpenRouter public models list
how_to_parse: GET works with no key (confirmed: HTTP 200, no auth). However the response only contains id/name/context_length/pricing/architecture - there is no tokens/s or latency field, so it cannot serve the 'speed' skill. Not used as a scores.csv source for this reason (would need the separate, keyed /rankings or Artificial Analysis feed for throughput).
license_or_terms_note: No key/login needed to call this endpoint, but it carries no benchmark scores, so excluded from scores.csv.

name: lmarena.ai leaderboard web UI (direct site, not the HF dataset mirror)
how_to_parse: n/a - the live site renders via client-side JS and does not expose a plain-GET JSON/CSV endpoint we could find. We use the official lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset Hugging Face dataset instead (see lmarena_text/lmarena_webdev/lmarena_agent/lmarena_text_style_control above), which is published by the same org and is the authoritative machine-readable form of this data.
